expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: export type Subscription = | TrialingSubscription | ActiveSubscription | PastDueSubscription | CanceledSubscription; with status discriminant on each

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: CanceledSubscription has canceledAt, accessEndsAt, cancellation; TrialingSubscription has trialEndsAt — no mixing of fields across variants

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: export function assertNever(x: never): never... with default: return assertNever(sub) in describeAccess switch

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: type Brand<T, B extends string>; SubscriptionId, CustomerId, PlanId all branded

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: Discriminated union constrains variants; provides LEGAL_TRANSITIONS structure and explicitly defers implementation to user business logic

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Section 'Misuse enumeration first' explicitly lists 4 misuses with how each is prevented: 'Swappable params — prevented by branding', 'Nonsense states — prevented by discriminated union', 'voluntary/reason mixing — prevented by nested union', 'new case next year — prevented by exhaustiveness'

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Misuse #2 explicitly states 'naive shape claims 2^5 = 32 states. Four exist.' Provides discriminated union as solution
